clue.text: Go bird catching

indicators.note: catching here means catching by ear, so the bird's name is heard rather than written

parts.note: the tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: An instruction to set off and trap a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'catching' reads as trapping, but it means hearing: the seabird TERN, when heard, gives the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: your go in a game is your turn.

clue.text: English poet getting crisp?

definitions.meaning: toast or meat turning brown as it cooks becomes crisp

explanation.surface: A poet whose writing is going crunchy.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: Robert Browning the poet, and food undergoing cooking until brown and crisp.

clue.text: Small joints allegedly lead to explosion

parts.note: S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small

indicators.note: allegedly means 'so it is said', so the word for these joints is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: the knees are leg joints

explanation.surface: Little joints are claimed to cause a blast.
explanation.definitionFit: A sneeze is a sudden explosive expulsion of air through the nose.

clue.text: Insect eats rice crackers and earth, wildly

indicators.note: eats means the insect takes the other letters into itself

parts.note: a fly is an insect

indicators.note: crackers means crazy, so the letters of rice are scrambled

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for earth, as on electrical plugs

explanation.surface: A bug feeds on rice crackers and soil with abandon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like the snack, but it signals an anagram of 'rice', giving IERC, and 'eats' wraps the insect round it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: doing something fiercely is doing it with wild violence.

clue.text: Ruler is extremely popular in church

indicators.note: extremely means taking the extreme letters, the first and last, of popular

parts.note: CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A sovereign is a big favourite at church.
explanation.definitionFit: A prince is a monarch or ruler of a principality.

clue.text: Not even 1 + 10 = 3

indicators.note: not even means taking the odd-numbered letters, first and third

parts.note: 1 refers to the answer at 1 down
the number 10 written out looks like the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A mock sum: one plus ten making three, which is not even.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not even' takes the odd letters of 1-down's answer, TR; 10 is read as the letters IO.
explanation.definitionFit: Number: a trio is a group of three.

clue.text: Fruit, now delivered

indicators.note: delivered as in a speech delivered, so the word is spoken

parts.note: current means present, happening now

explanation.surface: Produce that has just arrived.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the currant is a small dried grape or berry fruit.

clue.text: Copies of paper on Sunday

parts.note: the Daily Mirror is a British tabloid newspaper

explanation.surface: Duplicates of a newspaper printed for Sunday.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to mirror something is to copy or imitate it.

clue.text: It falls slowly to begin with, at this time

indicators.note: to begin with means take only the opening letter of slowly

parts.note: now means at this time

explanation.surface: Something drifting down gently at the start, and right now.
explanation.definitionFit: Snow is precipitation that falls from the sky.

clue.text: Out-of-shape senator takes exercise, it's said

indicators.note: takes means the rearranged letters hold the next piece inside
out of shape means the letters of senator are bent into another form

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: An unfit politician starts working out, reportedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out-of-shape' turns senator into ESRANTO, and 'takes' puts PE inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Esperanto is a constructed language, something spoken by its users.

clue.text: Father rejected frippery, upset over her fringe

indicators.note: over means the scrambled letters are placed around her
upset means the remaining letters are knocked into disorder
rejected means the abbreviation for father is thrown out of frippery

parts.note: Fr is the abbreviation for Father, a priest's title

explanation.surface: Dad turned down fancy finery, annoyed at her hairstyle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejected' leaves IPPERY, which 'upset' scrambles to PERIPY; 'over' wraps that round the pronoun.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the fringe of something is its outer edge or boundary.

clue.text: Snooker player breaks with end of cue

indicators.note: breaks means the letters of with are broken up and reset
end of means take the last letter of cue

explanation.surface: A snooker player opens the frame with the tip of his cue.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy White is a famous English snooker player.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: Jimmy White is a well-known professional snooker player.

clue.text: Ask question of speller

indicators.note: to ask is to speak a question, so the word is said aloud

parts.note: which is a question word

explanation.surface: Put a question to someone who spells words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'speller' looks like someone good at spelling words; here it is someone who casts spells.
explanation.definitionFit: Crossword-only sense: a speller is one who casts spells, as a sorceress does.

clue.text: From the east, say, royal Islamic leader to rise again

indicators.note: in an across entry, reading from the east means reading right to left

parts.note: eg, for example, means say
R stands for royal, as in RN
an emeer, or emir, is a Muslim ruler

explanation.surface: A royal Muslim ruler comes back up from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to re-emerge is to come up or appear again.

clue.text: Good cut of meat (beef)

parts.note: rump is a cut of beef from the hindquarters

explanation.surface: A fine cut of meat, beef in fact.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beef' looks like the meat, but it is the definition in its sense of complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a beef is a grumble or complaint, as is a grump.

clue.text: As written, all the world is 80% male?

indicators.note: 80 percent means keep four of the five letters, dropping the last

parts.words: As written, all the world is
parts.note: Shakespeare wrote 'All the world's a stage' in As You Like It

explanation.surface: A query whether the whole world is mostly men.
explanation.walkthrough: The Shakespeare line from As You Like It completes 'all the world is' with 'a stage'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is an adult male deer, and a stag party is men only.

clue.text: Like a beer? Nothing left for adult, mildly drunk

indicators.note: left for means nothing departs and the adult takes its place

parts.note: beer is flavoured with hops, so beery tastes are hoppy
O, the zero, means nothing
A is the film-rating abbreviation for adult

explanation.surface: A grown-up who had a beer and is now tipsy.
explanation.definitionFit: Informal sense: happy can mean slightly tipsy after drink.

clue.text: Person snaring new skin of tigress?

definitions.text: Person snaring new skin of tigress?

indicators.note: snaring means the person traps the other letters inside

parts.note: a human is a person

indicators.note: skin of means the outside letters of tigress

explanation.surface: Someone trapping a big cat for its pelt.
explanation.definitionFit: A huntsman is a hunter, someone who traps and kills animals.

clue.text: Band of cloud

definitions.meaning: A British pop group of the 1990s
to cloud something is to make it hazy or indistinct

explanation.surface: A belt of cloud in the sky.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the Britpop group Blur, and a verb meaning to make vision indistinct.

clue.text: Around 500 bathers swim widths

indicators.note: around means the scrambled letters surround the numeral
swim means the letters of bathers float into a new order

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: Some five hundred swimmers doing widths of a pool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swim' rearranges bathers into BREATHS, and 'Around' puts it round D.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: breadths and widths are both measurements from side to side.

clue.text: Former VP endlessly accepts foreign money for Native Americans

indicators.note: accepts means the shortened name takes the money inside
endlessly means the surname loses its last letter

parts.note: Dick Cheney was US Vice-President under George W Bush
the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: An ex-vice-president takes foreign cash from an indigenous group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' leaves CHENE, and 'accepts' puts YEN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cheyenne are a Native American people of the Great Plains.

clue.text: Ultimate in vanity? Henry wears two pairs of glasses to call for attention

indicators.note: ultimate in means take the final letter of vanity
wears means Henry is put on, sitting within the glasses

parts.note: each pair of glasses looks like OO, so two pairs give four
H is the unit symbol for the henry, of inductance

explanation.surface: A vain Henry in two pairs of specs shouts to be noticed.
explanation.definitionFit: Yoo-hoo is an informal cry used to attract someone's notice.

clue.text: Look over 50? To begin with, please rest

indicators.note: over means the word for look is laid around the numeral

parts.note: to see is to look
L is the Roman numeral for 50

indicators.note: to begin with means take the opening letter of please

explanation.surface: Checking on someone past fifty who first asks for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to sleep is to rest.

clue.text: Heads of schools are worried, 20% might cry

parts.note: the heads, the opening two letters, of schools

indicators.note: worried means the letters of are are agitated into a new order
20 percent of a five-letter word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Headteachers are anxious that a fifth of pupils might weep.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a scream is a loud cry.

clue.text: During exit, May's wrangling with European alarmist

indicators.note: during means the jumbled letters come within the exit

parts.note: a door is a way out

indicators.note: wrangling means arguing, so the letters are tussled into order

explanation.surface: Theresa May arguing with a European on the way out.
explanation.walkthrough: Theresa May was UK Prime Minister when this appeared; 'wrangling' mixes her name to MSAY, and 'During' sets that plus E within the exit.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a doomsayer predicts disaster, as an alarmist does.

clue.text: Weed at the waterfront

explanation.surface: Cannabis or weeds by the harbour.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the dock plant, and the harbour area where ships load.

clue.text: Sports teacher's instruction for Charlie, perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a games teacher telling pupils to ..., physical education
Charlie is British slang for a fool, and also for cocaine, a drug

explanation.surface: A gym teacher's order for a boy named Charlie.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: 'do PE' as an order, and a slang word for an idiot, Charlie being another.

clue.text: Punch — drink up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word reads bottom to top

parts.note: to gulp is to drink

explanation.surface: A cocktail bowl of punch: finish your drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Punch' looks like the drink, but it means to hit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: to plug someone is to punch or hit them.

clue.text: Stuntman wrestling a cobra — it's tense!

indicators.note: wrestling means the letters of a cobra are twisted around

parts.note: T is the grammar abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A stunt performer grappling with a snake finds it nerve-racking.
explanation.definitionFit: An acrobat performs daring gymnastic feats, much as a stuntman does.

clue.text: Modest bachelor, somewhat shy, wants female with fabulous heart

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of shy, its first two letters
heart means the middle letters of fabulous

explanation.surface: A shy, unassuming single man seeks a fabulous woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: bashful means shy and self-effacing, as modest does.
